rounds.text: Mahamaya Steel Industries Ltd trades at an exorbitant valuation that finds zero justification in its financial reality, carrying a trailing P/E of 156x and a price-to-book ratio of 8.68x [E1, E2]. This extreme multiple is further magnified when compared against sector benchmarks, with the company's 170.98x P/E and 10.34x P/B towering over sector medians of 24.92x and 2.39x respectively [E6, E7]. An EV/EBITDA multiple of 63.61x similarly dwarfs the 16.63x sector benchmark, underlining a severe market overpricing [E11]. Fundamental intrinsic value modeling paints an equally alarming picture, placing fair value at Rs 223 per share against the market price of Rs 782, which creates a negative margin of safety of -250.4% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that today's market price demands an aggressive 35.8% earnings growth rate, doubling the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E47]. Investors receive no income cushion while paying these inflated prices, as the dividend yield sits squarely at 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: [E56].
